query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: How the airline handles disruptions (delays, cancellations) is a genuine aspect OF service quality — the service dimension during irregular operations.

per_column.name: staff_behavior_tone
per_column.rationale: The demeanor/tone of staff is a constitutive interpersonal aspect of service quality.

per_column.name: crew_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Crew responsiveness is an aspect of service quality, but it overlaps heavily with staff_behavior_tone — both capture the human/staff-interaction dimension, weakening mutual exclusivity.

per_column.name: customer_service_resolution
per_column.rationale: How service issues are resolved is an aspect of service quality, though it overlaps conceptually with disruption_handling_quality (both concern problem handling/resolution).

per_column.name: aircraft_type_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Whether the operated aircraft differs from the advertised one is an operational/product attribute that may PREDICT dissatisfaction but is not itself an aspect of service quality; it is external to the service-quality concept.

judge.rationale: Four of five added columns are genuine facets of service quality, but the set skews heavily toward the human/staff and problem-handling dimensions. staff_behavior_tone and crew_responsiveness substantially overlap (both about staff interaction quality), and disruption_handling_quality and customer_service_resolution overlap (both about issue/problem resolution), lowering mutual exclusivity. Exhaustiveness is moderate-to-low because the tangible/physical service dimensions already present conceptually (seat comfort, food & beverage, inflight entertainment, cleanliness, boarding/check-in efficiency) are not represented among the added facets, so the decomposition covers only the interpersonal and disruption-handling slices of the concept. aircraft_type_mismatch is not a facet at all.
